passages.section: Israel rejections — Reasons for their rejection 1-13
passages.text:
Israel rejections
Reasons for their rejection 1-13
    - Did not feel need for salvation
        - Thought they were fine, save themselves
    - Zealous for God
        - Made own traditions and worshipped them
    - Proud and self righteous
        - Refused to listen and learn
    - Misunderstood their own law
        - “Law was a signpost, but could not take them to their destination…it only leads the sinner to the savior”
        - The law cannot only be outwardly obeyed, has to be obeyed in the heart as well
        - Is there a difference between obeying the Lord and calling on the Lord?

Remedy for Rejection 14-17
    - Used for missionary program
    - Is believing and obeying interchangeable?
    - To believe one must first hear

Results of their rejection 18-21
    - Israel is guilty
        - Israel DID hear
    - Message is shared with Gentiles due to Israel rejection
    - God still yearns for His people

passages.section: Romans 12 has the fourth “therefore” in Romans
passages.text:
Romans 12 has the fourth “therefore” in Romans
    - Romans 3:20 is the “therefore” of condemnation - the whole world is guilty before God
    - Romans 5:1 is the “therefore” of justification
    - Romans 8:1 is the “therefore” of assurance
    - Romans 12:1 is the “therefore” of dedication
        - The basis for the other relationships that the author discussed in this section

passages.section: Dedication - 3 steps > Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God
passages.text:
Your body is a living sacrifice to give to God
    - Two living sacrifices in the Bible
        - Isaac (Genesis 22)
            - Would have died in obedience to God, but ram took his place
                - Still counts, he died to self and willingly yielded to God’s will
        - Jesus Christ (Gospels)
            - Actually died in sacrifice

passages.section: Dedication - 3 steps > Your mind is a sacrifice to God
passages.text:
Your mind is a sacrifice to God
    - The world wants to change your mind with external pressure, the Holy Spirit changes your mind by releasing power within
        - If the world is in control, you are a conformer, if God controls your thinking, you are a transformer
        - In spending time meditating on God’s Word, memorization, part of inner spirit, God will make you more spiritual

passages.section: Dedication - 3 steps > Your will is a sacrifice to God
passages.text:
Your will is a sacrifice to God
    - Your mind controls your body, your will controls your mind
    - “Willpower” often fails, yielding our will to God to let His power takeover gives us willpower (and “won’t power”)
        - Surrender happens through disciplined prayer
        - “Not my will, but thy will be done”
    - Pray about EVERYTHING - yield plans of the day to Him

Honest evaluation
    - Each Christian must identify the spiritual gifts and ministry (or ministries) one is called to, ideally in a local church
    - Be honest (do not under or over evaluate oneself)
        - Both are examples of pride

Faithful cooperation
    - Even if you don’t like others or “don’t get along” - work with them
    - No one gift is better or greater than others
    - Gifts are tools to build with, not toys to play with or weapons to fight with

Loving participation
    - Attitude matters
    - Love is the circulatory system of the spiritual body
        - Have it be an honest love, not hypocritical love, humble and not proud
        - Romans 12:12 - Be JOYFUL in hope, PATIENT in affliction, and FAITHFUL in prayer
        - Share the burdens of others

Relationship (to enemies)
    - To return good in exchange for the evil we are met with, it requires love
        - There is a difference in having enemies because we are inpatient and lack love versus following Christ
    - How do we view revenge? Do we position ourselves as better / less deserving of “justice” than others? Do we view justice as love?

passages.section: Commentary Used: Wiersbe commentary — Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms:
passages.text:
Commentary Used: Wiersbe commentary
Romans 8 covers four spiritual freedoms:
    - 8:1-4 - Freedom from Judgment (No condemnation)
    - 8:5-17 - Freedom from Defeat (No obligation; because we cannot save ourselves, submit to God)
    - 8:18-30 - Freedom from Discouragement (No Frustration)
    - 8:31-39 (No Separation)

passages.section: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Creation groans (18-22)
passages.text:
Creation groans (18-22)
    - Suffering is a result of Adam’s sin, but it is not useless
    - The groans are compared to a woman in labor, pain now, but something beautiful is the result and the pain ends. It is worth it
        - Verse 22
    - Embrace today’s sufferings to build up to tomorrow
        - Example: Physical fitness
            - You BREAK down your body (often it is willingly) and embrace pain to be BUILT back up STRONGER
    - EVERYONE suffers
        - But not everyone has the same solution, and not all solutions are equal

passages.section: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Believers groan (23-25)
passages.text:
Believers groan (23-25)
    - We have a taste of glory to come, but anxious to get there
    - Adoption = redemption of body when Jesus comes back
        - There is a “climax” to adoption. The adoption begins when we are saved, the conversion when “the Spirit of adoption” comes and we receive the Holy Spirit. The “climax” is likened to the Rapture when we are called up and receive our glorified bodies
            - Example: When we are first saved, it is like an agreement to be adopted. The rapture and “climax” is when the child actually moving into the home
    - We as Believers still have hope as we know the climax of that adoption is coming

passages.section: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Holy Spirit groans (23-30) > Jesus groaned when He saw what sin did to mankind (Mark 7:34, John 11:33, 38)
passages.text: Jesus groaned when He saw what sin did to mankind (Mark 7:34, John 11:33, 38)

passages.section: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Holy Spirit groans (23-30) > The Spirit groans, but also prays on our behalf - ACTION
passages.text:
The Spirit groans, but also prays on our behalf - ACTION
    - We do not know God’s will or what to pray for, but the Spirit intercedes for us to “share the burden”. We are not only called to suffer with with Him, He shares our burden

passages.section: Romans 8:18-30 discusses suffering and pain, and how we are now free from discouragement > Three groans are mentioned > Holy Spirit groans (23-30) > God is always at work (verse 28) and has a perfect plan (verse 29) for those who love Him and are called according to His purpose
passages.text:
God is always at work (verse 28) and has a perfect plan (verse 29) for those who love Him and are called according to His purpose
    - This verse is often taken out of context, “for those who love God” and “for those who are called according to his purpose” is CRITICAL and is sometimes left out when this verse is referenced
    - Predestination applies only to saved people (??? - Point to be discussed with broader group)
        - God does not predestined people to be eternally condemned

passages.section: Closing / Reflecting Question - Faith, hope, and love — 1 Corinthians 13:13 - “And now these three remain: faith, hope, and love. But the greatest of these is love”. Do you have all three? Do you have hope? — Hebrews 11:1 - Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen
